name: Frostbite
lede: Frostbite is a hot, bluish pink, a Crayola-list name whose swatch has little to do with the medical condition it is named for.

sections.title: A crayon name
sections.body: Our library lists Frostbite among the Crayola names and finds no earlier origin [1]. The date and the person who chose it are undocumented in our data. The nearest ISCC-NBS block is deep purplish pink, about 9.3 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale, so the swatch is a loose fit even to that standard name [1].

sections.title: What frostbite looks like
sections.body: The name suggests cold, but the skin has other colors. A medical list in Birren's survey of color in diagnosis describes frostbite as skin that turns whiter than normal, then passes to dark red, reddish or reddish-black [2]. The pink here is nothing like that sequence, and it sits closer to [[hot-pink]] and [[magenta]] than to anything a clinic would record [1][2]. Treat the name as branding, not description.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering even 1 per cent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes our archive, not painting as a whole [3]. The hex is also a screen approximation of a printed crayon wax, not a measured pigment [1].
